Text.Text: Rhee is answered for, and the bunker runs Republic drills again. I have stopped testing you. If you noticed, you will also have noticed I never say that. Carry it well, commander.
Rank 50 in Leadership, then report back. You need people who trust your orders before I can ask you to challenge mine.

My old adjutant has kept the Republic Engineering Bunker on Viscara and the garrison inside it. Six Decisive Command adepts are drilling obedience through fear. Defeat the six and recover their bunker docket. I want the orders they've been following in front of me.
Take the bunker key to its entrance on the Republic combat deck. Keep your people together as you enter. Bring me that docket.

A decision is a weapon the same way a blade is: it only cuts if it arrives. Decisive command means your order lands before fear does - yours or theirs. Hesitate, and fear gives the order instead, and fear is a mutineer by nature. I hate hesitation more than error. An error can be corrected by the next order. Hesitation teaches the room there might not be one.

Halden Rhee. Twelve years my adjutant, and the finest executor of orders I ever signed for. When I retired, the Republic gave him the bunker to decommission. Instead he sealed it and built a chain of command that answers to him alone. The soldiers inside are not evil. They are obedient - which is worse, because it is almost the virtue I taught them.

The docket is their operations record - watch rotations, drill schedules, punishment details. Every order Rhee has issued since he went dark, countersigned by officers who should have refused. It is evidence, and it is a map of who below deserves a court and who deserves a grave. Bring it to me intact.
Six adepts in the Republic Engineering Bunker. Bring their docket back to the combat deck. I want names and orders.
That folder under your arm has a Republic spine. Hand it over and stand easy while I read.

Countersigned, every page. Some of these names I trained... and two I will ask you about another day. You executed the order as given, on time, without theater. That is rarer than courage. Draw your pay and stay close - the next order is already written.

Five specialists are holding the bunker shield grid. Those shields used to cover an evacuation; now they keep the garrison in. Defeat the five and bring me the relay. I'll find out whose orders made that change.
Break their drill rather than joining it. The relay comes back to the combat deck.

It is - and I am glad you said it, because heroes never do. I sent heroes out alone twice in my career, and I wrote both eulogies. Heroes hesitate for an audience; teams do not. Take at least one steady gun down there and practice being obeyed. The bunker is a better classroom than any parade ground.

The relay is a fist-sized Republic component that decides where the shield's power goes. Rhee cannot replace it - the pattern is licensed to the engineering corps, and the corps thinks the bunker is empty. Take it, and his screen is a memory. It is also proof for my report. Mutineers with a live shield grid are a fortress. Mutineers without one are criminals in a basement.

Rhee's veterans - the ones who sealed the door with him on the first day. They hold their posts the way I taught them to: in pairs, overlapping arcs, no gaps for sentiment. Expect discipline, not madness. And expect them to test your voice. They have obeyed one man for years, and part of every one of them is waiting to hear whether yours carries further.
Five specialists hold the bunker's shield relay. Defeat them and return the relay to me.
The glow over the bunker died last night. If the relay is in your pack, the fortress problem is over and the criminal problem is all that is left. Let me see it.

Republic stamp, corps pattern, carbon on the contacts - you pulled it live. Good. The screen is down and Rhee knows it, which means the easy stages are over. You have stopped being an errand and started being a threat. He will treat you accordingly. So will I, and from me that is promotion.

Vhon enforces the adjutant's orders. Challenge her in the Engineering Bunker, defeat her, and recover her command crest. Take people who can act while you're under pressure. She learned that part of command well enough.
Call Vhon at the Engineering Bunker's challenge marker. Move decisively when the opening comes. Recover the crest and come back with the people you brought.

Vhon was my breach officer. Where other captains planned, she decided - the door opened and she was already through it, and her people followed because following her was safer than thinking. Rhee promised her a command with no committees and no court-martials for being right too fast. I understand why she took it. I will still hold the door at her funeral.
I'm advising you, not barring the door. A breach goes better when someone covers the person moving through it. Vhon knows how to punish the moment you can't do both. Take support if you can.

The crest was the bunker's commission - the Republic's mark of command, worn by whoever answered for the garrison. Rhee cracked it in front of the assembled ranks and said the Republic's half was dead weight. He gave the split thing to Vhon like a medal. Bring it back, and the Republic's half starts weighing something again.
Call Vhon at the bunker's challenge marker. Defeat her, recover the crest, and bring your people home.
You are standing straighter and your people are alive - that tells me the door is open before you say it. The crest. Let me see what he did to it.

Split clean through the emblem... he always did have precise hands. I will wear it cracked until this ends; mended honors lie. Vhon deserved a better war and a worse commander, and you gave her the cleanest ending on offer. Two links of his chain are cut. What remains is the circle that runs his supply, and then the man whose voice all of it obeys.
Four officers still control the bunker's supplies. Their override chip keeps the garrison dependent on them. Defeat the four and recover it. Nobody should have to obey an order just to eat.
Recover the chip. Then we can see what obedience looks like when the quartermaster stops enforcing it.

Understand what you have taken from him so far. The docket proved his orders. The relay was his wall. The crest was his claim to legitimacy. The chip is his ability to feed the people who obey him. After tonight, every soldier in that bunker will know their next meal depends on the Republic's mercy and not on Rhee's signature. Watch how fast obedience remembers its oath.

Two of the four came from my old command - Puren, who could route supply through a war zone in his sleep, and Task, who never once filed late. The other two are Rhee's inventions, promoted for loyalty and taught to count second. Do not rank them by their paperwork. In those vaults, all four will fight like the food depends on it. It does.

Expect the discipline of people who know exactly how many rounds sit on every shelf around them. They will spend ammunition like misers, make you bleed for corners, and fall back through doors they have rehearsed. Bring the team from the breach - rested, fed, and drilled on your voice. Store rooms forgive nothing done alone.
Four officers in the bunker have the override chip. Return it after they're defeated.
If the vaults have gone quiet, then it is done, and the thing in your pocket outranks every officer left down there. Hand it over.

The override chip. With this, the Republic decides who eats in that bunker - which means the garrison's obedience is already looking for a new home. You have unmade his chain of command link by link, and you did it my way: no theater, no speeches, orders executed as issued. One door remains. Behind it is the voice all of this obeyed. Sleep first, commander. That is an order.

The master commands from the Engineering Command Room. Call him at its challenge marker and defeat him. Keep your own plan when he starts issuing orders. Then report to me here on the combat deck. This command needs a proper end.

Last briefing, then. Do not try to out-shout him - you cannot, and volume was never the point. Give your orders to your own people and let him give his to a garrison that no longer eats, hides, or believes at his word. You have spent four errands cutting his voice away from its echoes. In that room, finish the argument: two commands, one door, and the one that holds is the one with an oath still in it.

His last order - the last one I obeyed? A sealing drill, years ago, a raid scare. He called seal-and-hold half a second before the confirmation came through, and he was right, and I countersigned it. That half second is the whole tragedy. He learned the confirmation was optional. Every order since has been given on no authority but his own reflexes, and the garrison obeyed because obeying him had always been right before. The mutiny did not begin with treason. It began with applause.

Afterward, the garrison surrenders. I know those soldiers; they are waiting for permission. The Republic reoccupies the bunker, the courts sort the countersigners, and the docket you brought me decides who was coerced. And I file my last report, which will say that decisive command survived Halden Rhee because someone learned it clean. I do not put names in reports lightly. Yours will be in this one.

He decides before most people have finished being afraid. He's done it so long that the reason for deciding has stopped mattering to him. Keep your own plan, give your own orders, and listen to the people he would tell you to ignore.
The Engineering Command Room has the master's challenge marker. Defeat him and report back to the combat deck.
The bunker went quiet before dawn - garrison-quiet, surrender-quiet. I have waited years to hear it. Report.

His last order is answered. Take the pay and see to whoever stood with you. When you're ready to study Decisive Command, I'll teach you what my adjutant forgot: the people who follow you are the reason to decide well. Dismissed.
Run the briefing again.
On my way. You'll have the docket.
What is decisive command, to you?
Who turned your bunker?
What is in this docket you want so badly?
Not yet. I don't take orders I can't execute today.
Your docket. Every page intact.
Give me the grid briefing again.
The shield comes down. You have my word.
This sounds like more than one gun's work.
What exactly is the relay?
What kind of soldiers am I facing?
Not yet. My squad isn't ready.
One relay, pulled live. Your fortress is a basement now.
Take me through the breach again.
We'll take the door as one motion. All of us.
Who is Captain Vhon?
Why do you recommend support?
What is the story behind the crest?
Not yet. I won't spend a team I haven't drilled.
The crest, off her shoulder. She met us head-on, like you said.
Go over the stores again.
Four quartermasters. The chip comes home.
What does the chip actually cut?
Who am I killing down there?
How will they fight in the vaults?
Not yet. My people need food and sleep - you taught me that math.
The override chip. The vaults answer to the Republic now.
Brief me on Rhee once more.
Then we take his door together, and his last order dies in that room.
Where did it start? What turned him?
What happens to the garrison when he falls?
How do I fight a voice I want to obey?
Not yet. When we go, we go rested and in force.
It's done. His room is silent, and everyone I brought walked out of it.
